title: jobspec-reference/1.0.0
description: How Eval-lab names a JobSpec it does not hold. Agent-workbench owns the JobSpec format; this schema describes the *reference* to one, never the JobSpec itself. It deliberately carries no task description, no prompt, no repository contents, no test command output, no credentials and no hidden-test material: everything here is either a digest or a field that is already public on both sides of the boundary. A reader who wants the JobSpec must ask Agent-workbench for the bytes whose sha256 is jobspec_digest, and can then prove they got the right ones.

schema_version.description: Pinned. A reference declaring any other version is rejected rather than reinterpreted, because a consumer that guesses at an unknown version is how two sides come to disagree silently about a field.

jobspec_id.description: Agent-workbench's opaque identifier. Never parsed for meaning.

jobspec_digest.description: sha256 over the exact JobSpec bytes Agent-workbench serialised. This is the identity of the job; the id is only a label.

jobspec_format_version.description: The version of Agent-workbench's own JobSpec format. Recorded so a digest stays interpretable later; Eval-lab does not validate against it.

task_kind.description: The one public classification Eval-lab is allowed to see. It selects which deterministic checks apply and nothing else.

retry_budget.description: How many attempts the job was permitted. Public because attempt lineage cannot be checked for boundedness without it.

declared_visible_test_command.description: The visible-test command Agent-workbench says it ran. Recorded for provenance and never executed by Eval-lab: a command string that arrives with the evidence is untrusted input, not an instruction.
